O. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 11 ) was adop:ed by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 July 1982, after the draft fidized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Comx=ittee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Coucil. Fast development in the field of instrunxnts has brought a significant change in their basic contem and deign, It has been felt over the years that IS : 2352-1363* does not cater for the present day needs of the instruments and is also not in lime with `Ae recent trends in climatic and environmental testing procedures to be aiopted for improving their It has, therefore, 3ecome necessary to have quality and reliability. uniform and more rational testing procedures as far as possible. This series of standards on climatic and duraH.ity tests ( 1S : 10236 ) has been prepared with this objective.
0.2

Standard 0.2.1 It is proposed to withdraw the existing Indian ( IS :2352-1 963* ) as soon as the [ests mextioned therein are covered in the new series ( IS : 10236 ). 0.3 This stanadard deals with dry heat teits applicable both for high temperature use and storage, with and withom thermal shock.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part II ) covers the procedure for conducting heat test for optical instruments.

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard the definitions given in IS : 10236 ( Part [ )* shall apply.
3. OBJECT

3.1 The object of the dry heat test is to determine the suitability of optical instrument for use and/or storage at high temperature appropriate to the required severity.
4. INITIAL

MEASUREMENTS

4.1 The instrument shall be visually examined and optically, electrically and mechanically checked as required by the relevant instrument specification.
5. TEST

CHAMBER meet the requirements

5.1 The chamber used for this test shall specified in 5.1.1 to 5.1.8.

5.1.1 The chamber shall be capable of maintaining its working space at any high temperature as desired by the required severity with a tolerance of A 3�C. 5.1.2 The relative humidity shall not exceed 50 percent. by a

5.1.3 The temperature in the chamber shall be monitored temperature sensing device suitably located in its working space.

5.1.4 The air in the chamber shall be continuously agitated but not vigorously. Necessary care shall be taken to ensure that the conditions throughout the chamber are homogeneous and are as near as possible to those prevailing in the immediate vicinity of the sensing device. 5.1.5 The specimen under test shall not be subjected to direct radiation from the heating element of the chamber. 5.1.6 Care shall be taken that any heat dissipation of the specimen unri er test shall not appreciably influence the conditions in the chamber. 5.1.7 The chamber shall have provision to supply the specimen under test from an external source. electric power to

5.1.8 The chamber shall have a provision for a suitable viewing window to see the functioning of the instrument, as and when required. q Procedure for c1imat ic and durability tests for optical

SEVERITIES

7. TEST

PROCEDL= I -- Test without therrmd shock for high temperature use. instrument shall be subjected to this test in the unpacked

7.1 Msthod 7.1,1 The condition.

7.1.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument under test shall be introduced into the chamber. The temperature of the chamber shall then be raised to the severity as specified in relevant instrument specification, at a rate not exceeding 5'C per 5 minutes.

7.1.3 On attaining the temperature equilibrium, if required by the relevant instrument specification, the electrical/electronic arrangement, if fitted in the instrument, shall be switched on to check whether it is shall bz functioning or not. .if~er this verification the arrangemmt switched off. 7.1.4 Aher attainin~ the temperature equilibrium t2e instrument shall remain at the temperature appropriate to the severity for 16 hours Or such other period as may be spdied in the relevaat instrument specification. 7.1.5 At the end of the period of exmsure, if required by the relevant instrument specification the electrical/electronic arrangement fitted in the instrument shall b~ switched on and its functioning seen. 7.1.6 At the end or the test, the chamber shaH be swlched off and allowe 3 to cool down to the temperature as specified in the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery. 7.L7 Rtco~ery -- The instrument shall then be remumd from the chamber and kept tm ier standard a~mospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hcmr nor more than two hours. 7.2 M sthod 11 -- Tes; without storage. thermal shock for high temperature

7.2.1 The instrument shall be subjected to th;s test in the unpacked condition. 7.2.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument under test shall be introduced into the chamber. The temperature of the chamber shall then be raised to the severity as specified in the relevant instrument specification, at a rate not exceeding 5'C per 5 minutes. 7.2.3 After temperature equilibrium has been attained the instrument shall remain at the high temperature appropriate to the severity for 96 hours or such other period as may be specified in the relevant instrument specification. 7.2.4 After that period the chamber shall be switched off and allo~ved to cooi to the temperature as specified in the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery. 7.2.5 Recovery -- The instrument shall then be removed from the chamber and kept under standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two hours. 7.3

Method

III -- Test with thermal shock for high temperature use.

7.3.1 The instrument shall be subjected to this test in the unpacked condition.
7.3.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument shall be introduced into the chamber which is maintained at the se~-erity required by the relevant instrument specification. 7.3.3 On attaining the temperature equilibrium, if required by the relevant instrument specification, the electrical/electronic arrangement, it is, if fitted in the instrument, shall be switched cm m check whether functioning or not. After this verification the arrangement shall be switched off. 7.3.4 After attaining the temperature equilibrium the instrument shall remain at the temperature appropriate to the se~-erit y for 16 hours or such other Ferlod as may be specified in the rele~-ant instrument. specification. 7.3.5 At the end of the period of exposure, if required by the relerant instrument specification, the electrical/electronic arran~ ement fittea in the instrument shall be switched on and its functioning seen. 7.3,6 The instrument shall then be remo~ed from the chamber and as required by the relevant instrument specification, its moving parts shall be examined at a temperature near to the specified severity. Signs of any flow of lubricant at the movable joints shall be carefully observed, particularly in instruments required for use by De fence Services. 6

7.4.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument shall be introduced into the chamber which is maintained at the severity required by the relevant instrument specification. 7.4.3 After temperature equilibrium has been attained the instrument to the severity for shall remain at the high temperature appropriate 96 hours or such other period as may be specified in the relevant instrument specification. 7.4.4 Recovery -- After that period the instrument shall be taken out of the chamber and kept at standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two hours. 8.
